source.title: Doubling constructions: Global functoriality for non-generic cuspidal representations
source.authors: Yuanqing Cai, Solomon Friedberg and Eyal Kaplan
source.version: arXiv v5, 20 May 2024, 60 pages; the Annals text was not fetched. Numbering from v5.

summary: Cai, Friedberg and Kaplan prove that every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), without assuming genericity. They use the converse theorem, with twisted L-functions controlled by the generalized doubling method (local γ-factors, their stability, and a global analysis of the doubling Eisenstein series). They deduce that the transfer is a coarse transfer at every place, and that local coarse transfers exist. Partial first extraction (cc-442dc5): the main theorems and definitions are items; the remaining lemmas and propositions of §3 and §4 are listed in the handoff.

items.name: Weak functorial transfer
items.statement: Π on GL_N(A) is a weak functorial transfer of an irreducible automorphic π of G(A) if at almost all finite places where π_ν is unramified, Π_ν is the local unramified transfer of π_ν via r_G, and at the infinite places the infinitesimal character of Π_ν is determined via r_G by that of π_ν.
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Converse Theorem of Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi
items.statement: An irreducible admissible Π = ⊗Π_ν of GL_N(A) with suitable central character and absolutely convergent L(s, Π) is quasi-automorphic when the twisted L-functions L(s, Π × τ) satisfy the conditions of [CKPSS01, §2].
items.note: Cited supplier; the exact twisting set and conditions are to be copied from §2.

items.name: Properties of the generalized doubling integral
items.statement: The local integral Z(s, ω, f) converges absolutely for Re(s) ≫ 0 and continues meromorphically, with the properties listed in Theorem 3.2 (from [CFK22]).

items.name: Characterization of the doubling γ-factor
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(G) and generic τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), γ(s, π × τ, ψ) satisfies and is characterized by the properties of Theorem 3.5, starting with unramified twisting γ(s, π × |det|^{s_1}τ, ψ) = γ(s + s_1, π × τ, ψ).
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Compatibility with the unramified transfer
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(G), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), with π unramified if F is non-archimedean, the γ-, L- and ε-factors of π × τ and T(π) × τ coincide.
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Holomorphy of tempered L-factors
items.statement: For π tempered (and unramified if F is non-archimedean) and τ generic: if τ is tempered, L(s, π × τ) is holomorphic in Re(s) > 0, with the unitary case as in Theorem 3.8(2); Corollary 3.9 gives the unitary variant.
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Stability of γ-factors
items.statement: Over a non-archimedean F, for π ∈ Irr(G) and Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) with central character χ_π, the γ-factors of π and Π twisted by a sufficiently highly ramified character agree (Theorem 3.10, from [CFK22, Lemma 7.3]).
items.note: Paraphrase; copy the exact statement in the next continuation.

items.name: Holomorphy of the Eisenstein series
items.statement: For τ unitary cuspidal on GL_k(A) and θ a unitary Hecke character (θ = 1 unless H = GSpin), if |·|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ for all real t, then E_{τ,θ,c}(h; s, f) is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 0.
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Functional equation and boundedness
items.statement: L(s, π × τ) = ε(s, π × τ)L(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨); if both sides are entire they are bounded in vertical strips.

items.name: Entireness of twisted L-functions
items.statement: For unitary cuspidal π on G(A) and τ on GL_k(A) satisfying the conditions of Theorem 4.8 (including |·|^{it}χ_π τ ≇ τ^∨ for all real t), L(s, π × τ) is entire.
items.note: Conclusion paraphrased; the full list of conditions is to be copied in the next continuation.

items.name: Weak functorial transfer of cuspidal representations
items.statement: Every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation π of G(A) has a weak functorial transfer Π to GL_N(A).
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Weak transfers are coarse transfers everywhere
items.statement: If Π is a weak functorial transfer of a cuspidal π of G(A), then Π_ν is a coarse transfer of π_ν at every place.
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

items.name: Existence of local coarse transfers
items.statement: Over a local field f, every π′ ∈ Irr(G(f)) has a coarse transfer to GL_N(f).
items.note: Statement as in the paper, with G a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group over a number field F (§1) and N the dimension of the standard representation of its dual.

routes.title: Automorphic L-functions and local factors, Part II: the generalized doubling method and functorial transfer for classical groups
routes.brief: Automorphic L-functions and local factors, extended to the generalized doubling method of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg and Kaplan for symplectic and quasi-split orthogonal groups twisted by GL_k: the local doubling integrals and their γ-, L- and ε-factors (characterization, unramified compatibility, holomorphy for tempered data, stability), the global Eisenstein series and functional equation, entireness of twisted L-functions, and the Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi converse theorem. Final theorems: every cuspidal representation of a classical group has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N, and local coarse transfers exist. Import local representation theory from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.
routes.reason: The doubling integrals, their local factors and the converse-theorem transfer extend the atlas's automorphic L-function roadmap.
